les: Die water begin nie by die kraan nie

The Conversation (https://theconversation.com/south-africa-has-had-lots-of-rain-and-most-dams-are-full-but-water-crisis-threat-persists-178788) covers falling dam levels in South African droughts. items.bewering: Die dam vul op sy eie tyd, nie op ons s'n nie. ... Die kraan is die einde van daardie lang pad en nie sy begin nie. (also the title: 'Die water begin nie by die kraan nie')
items.blok: Hoekom die water kan opraak
items.bron: Mapping checked against the chain the lesson itself describes and the sources above (rain, river, dam or ground, purification works, pipes, tap). A dam's level follows rainfall in its catchment, not what people use, and the tap is the last link. A learner reasoning further is led to 'rain far away decides how much I have', which is correct. The comparison does not suggest water is made at the tap or that a dam can be refilled on demand. Fresh check, this round.

items.bron: Stats SA General Household Survey (https://www.statssa.gov.za/publications/P0318/P03182025.pdf; summarised by Business Day, 27 May 2026). In 2023 about 45% of households had piped water in the dwelling, about 30% on site, 9.7% used communal taps, and 3.3% fetched water from rivers, streams, dams, wells and springs. Boreholes and tanks are listed source categories. Fresh check, this round.

items.bewering: dam: Water wat agter 'n muur of 'n grondwal dwars oor 'n rivier of stroom opgevang word.
items.blok: dam
items.bron: Britannica, Dam; Wikipedia, Embankment dam (earthfill walls); Wikipedia, Dam (agricultural reservoir): in South Africa 'dam' names both the barrier and the water behind it. The entry takes the water sense. The running text uses the same sense ('hou dit in 'n dam', 'Die dam vul', 'Die dam sak'), so the term means the same in the text as in the entry. Read alone, the entry does not fit anything it should not. Fresh check, this round.

items.blok: droogte
items.bron: Drought.gov and UNDRR MH0401 (as above): a prolonged period of below-normal precipitation. This matches the running text (''n Droogte duur lank en dit reën baie minder as gewoonlik') word for word in substance. Fresh check, this round.

items.bewering: suiweringswerk: Die plek waar water skoongemaak word voordat dit by die krane uitkom.
items.blok: suiweringswerk
items.bron: South African municipal usage of 'watersuiweringswerke' for drinking-water plants (George Herald; Netwerk24/Paarl Post 'boorgatwatersuiweringswerke'). The entry matches the running text ('gaan eers na 'n suiweringswerk waar dit skoongemaak word ... tot by die krane'). Note for a person, not a defect: the unqualified word 'suiweringswerke' is also common in South African usage for sewage works ('rioolsuiweringswerke'; e.g. National Archives, Stellenbosch 'Riolering en sanitasie. Uitbreiding van suiweringswerke'). The entry is true for the lesson's use but narrower than the word. Fresh check, this round.

items.blok: boorgat
items.bron: Wikipedia, Borehole (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borehole), and Homebuilding, What is a borehole: a narrow shaft drilled into the ground; a water borehole needs a pump because it is too narrow and deep to draw from by hand. This matches both uses in the running text. Fresh check, this round.

items.bewering: stormwaterdrein: Die gat in die straat wat reënwater van die pad af wegvat.
items.blok: stormwaterdrein
items.bron: City of Bothell, Stormwater Terminology (https://www.bothellwa.gov/1376/Stormwater-Terminology): a storm drain is 'an opening built into a curb or street and connected to a pipe to carry away stormwater'. The running text uses the same sense ('Wat in 'n stormwaterdrein beland') and then says where the water goes, so text and entry agree. Fresh check, this round.

items.bewering: verdamp: Wanneer water in die lug optrek en 'n nat plek daardeur droër word.
items.blok: verdamp
items.bron: USGS, Evaporation and the Water Cycle (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/evaporation-and-water-cycle), and National Geographic Education, Evaporation: liquid water becomes water vapour and moves into the atmosphere. Puddles and wet clothes dry because the water is not vanishing but going into the air. The entry simplifies without falsehood and matches the running text ('op 'n tuin gooi, verdamp gou'). Fresh check, this round.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.blok: kieme
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth, What Are Germs? (https://kidshealth.org/en/kids/germs.html): germs are 'tiny organisms, or living things, that can cause disease'. This is a shared wording a person has ruled stays, and it is not raised. The running text uses it in the same sense ('kieme ... kan 'n mens siek maak'). The entry says 'kan', not that every germ does. Fresh check, this round.

opsomming: All 42 claims in the lesson hold up against sources, every glossary term means the same thing in the running text as in its entry, the lesson has no eli10 block, and its one ranking word ('veral diarree') is true; a person may want to know that 'suiweringswerk' also commonly means a sewage works in South African Afrikaans, which is a word-choice question and not an error.
